content.text: Explore satellite orbits. Learn the definition of a satellite orbit and understand the types of orbits of satellites around Earth. See how fast satellites travel. FAQ How many orbits are there for satellites? There are three large groups of satellite orbits. Within these groups are multiple choices. One of the semi-synchronous orbits, for example, is the Molniya orbit. This orbit is slanted and elliptical. What are the different satellite orbits? There are three main types of orbits. A high Earth orbit is called a geosynchronous orbit. A semi-synchronous orbit is a middle Earth orbit. Low Earth orbits are the lowest orbits and require the greatest speed. A satellite is a body or object in space that orbits around a larger body, such as a planet. This object can be organic or human-made. The moon and the International Space Station both fit the description of a satellite because they both make orbital patterns around the Earth. Satellites are important objects in the context of space because by understanding them; scientists can understand the impact of gravity and velocity on each other. Human-made satellites provide even more information than simple data regarding gravity and velocity. They also gather information about nearby planets, stars, and formations in space. Scientists perform experiments, and telescopes provide images. The speed of satellites can affect how long it takes that satellite to complete one orbit around the planet. For example, it takes the moon of the Earth just over 27 days to complete a full orbit around the Earth. High Earth OrbitThe high Earth orbit group is referred to as geosynchronous orbits. One type of geosynchronous orbit is the geostationary orbit, in which a geosynchronous orbit is entered exactly above the equator. These orbits have the exact same schedule as their planet's axis. High Earth orbit satellites are important because they are used to monitor the activity of the sun. They also collect data on the weather in space. Other factors examined by high Earth satellites include magnetic fields and radiation levels. In addition to these functions, high Earth orbits can be used for telecommunications purposes. These satellites must stay in the exact same place above the Earth. Pertinent facts include: To unlock this lesson you must be a Study.com member Create an account A satellite is a body that fulfills orbits around a larger planet in the universe. They can be human-made or natural. The moon is a satellite around the Earth, as is the International Space Station. Satellite orbits are the patterns used by the satellite to orbit a planet. These orbits are affected by the pull of gravity and the velocity of the satellite. There are three main groups of satellite orbits: high, medium, and low Earth orbits. High Earth orbits, called geosynchronous orbits, are used by satellites that facilitate telecommunications and data collection. They must maintain a speed of approximately 3 kilometers per second. Low Earth orbits must maintain much higher speeds of around 8 kilometers per second. Medium Earth orbits are called semi-synchronous orbits. These orbits complete an orbit in half the time it takes for one planetary revolution. Semi-synchronous orbits include Molniya orbits. These are slanted and elliptical orbits that pass close to the Earth and also go far away from the Earth. Elliptical orbits are used to provide satellite communications capabilities that are higher than other orbits. Low Earth orbits are used by satellites that provide images of the Earth.
